results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and how real decks have played them.

The three cards have never been played together in a published list. Town Greeter's main home is Golgari Roots, Spider-Man's is Rogue, and Dimir Midrange shares blue and black with Spider-Man. I'll look at those shells and search the pool for mill and reanimation enablers.

The pool shows a clear route. Golgari Roots already runs Town Greeter, Overlord of the Balemurk, Molt Tender and Insidious Roots, and the mill-and-reanimate package supplies the graveyard that Bringer and Spider-Man need. I'll pull the latest Golgari Roots list and check the reanimation and mill cards I'd consider.

The Golgari Roots list is the proven mana base to borrow. Next I'll verify the removal, mill and dual-land candidates, since the blue splash for Superior Spider-Man depends on which lands are in Standard.

The three requested cards need black, green and blue, and I have verified every card I plan to use. Next I'll run a draft check on the Golgari shell with a one-card blue splash, and odds on finding a blue source for Spider-Man.

The check flags low green sources and says the deck wants about 24 lands. I'll move to 23 lands by cutting Deathcap Marionette and adding a Forest, then recheck.

Both checks pass with no errors or warnings. Before I write the sideboard, I'll verify the candidate sideboard cards against the field: artifact and enchantment hate for Vivi and Izzet, discard, and graveyard removal.

The sideboard targets the field: Dimir and Pixie's planeswalkers and creatures, Izzet's small creatures, and Vivi's artifacts and enchantments. Now I'll submit the deck with the win line and the card needs.

The submission was accepted in all other respects; only one card note came back. Honest Rutstein is rarely played in Standard, so I'll answer the note with its specific job in this deck.

I submitted a Golgari mill-and-reanimate brew with a one-card blue splash for Superior Spider-Man. The plan is Town Greeter and Overlord of the Balemurk to fill the graveyard and keep returning creatures, Spider-Man copying the best graveyard creature, and Bringer of the Last Gift as the late finisher at 8 mana. The 8-mana finisher makes this slow, and the win line only completes by turn 7 in about 7% of games, so expect a grindy deck that wins late.

I weighed three directions. I chose the Golgari shell because Town Greeter lives there, the mill and recursion package fuels both Bringer and Spider-Man, and Golgari Roots' mana base carries the deck. The alternatives were a Dimir build around Spider-Man, which has almost no graveyard fill and would splash green for a 2-drop, and a green-white Rogue build, which cannot cast Bringer's double black. Honest Rutstein drew a card note; I kept it because its return and its cost reduction (Bringer to 7, Spider-Man to 3) serve the finisher.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I built a Temur Landfall brew (green base, red and a light blue splash) around Mightform Harmonizer, Full Bore and Spell Snare, and the deck is submitted. No published list runs these three together, so it is a brew. I borrowed the Landfall shell's creatures and mana because Harmonizer's power doubling needs a steady stream of land drops.

I considered three directions: Temur Landfall, Simic Landfall with only a red splash for Full Bore, and Boros Aggro with Full Bore. I chose Temur because it is the only one where all three cards are in colors with a landfall package. Harmonizer warped on turn 4, then a land drop doubles it to 8 power, then Full Bore makes it an 11/6 haste trampler. Kicked Burst Lightning and a second warp hit close the game.

Two weak points to know about. Spell Snare is the weakest fit: it only counters mana value 2 spells, and the blue sources are thin (three real blue lands plus two fetches). Full Bore's haste and trample only work on a warped creature, and Harmonizer is the only warp creature in the deck, so the win line depends on it. I answered the submit check's warp-enabler concern with a needs reason rather than adding more warp creatures.

winLine.does: Turn 1 ramp: taps for G from turn 2 so turn-4 mana covers warp plus Full Bore.
Warped from hand for {2}{G} on turn 4 (3 lands + Elves before the land drop); exiled at end step, so it is a one-shot haste attacker.
Land drop after the warp: landfall trigger targets Harmonizer and doubles its power from 4 to 8; the land also gives the extra mana.
{R} on the warped Harmonizer: +3/+2 and, because it was warped, haste and trample. Harmonizer attacks as an 11/6 trampler.
Finishes: kicked for 4 to the face (or 2 unkicked) on the following turn, with a repeat warp-and-Full-Bore hit as the second threat.

results.text:

Build a board of Elementals, using Lavaleaper, Summon: Shiva and Ice Flan to get a 5+ mana value Elemental out. Once Ice Flan (MV 6) is out, Sunderflock costs about {1}{U}{U}. Its entry trigger returns the opponent's non-Elemental creatures to hand while the Elementals stay, and the 5/5 flyer finishes.

- The checker flagged Summon: Shiva as rarely played. I kept it because it is one of the few 5+ Elementals that lowers Sunderflock's cost, and its chapters I and II stun blockers.
- The win line in the submission is turn 7 (Ashling, Lavaleaper, Shiva, Ice Flan, then Sunderflock). The tool's draw simulation shows that line complete by turn 7 in only 1% of games, so treat it as a target rather than a reliable plan.

The plan: turn 2 Dark Ritual into Buried Alive to put Visara, Akroma and Phantom Nishoba in the graveyard. Turn 4 Living Death with Lotus Petal and four Swamps wipes the opponent's creatures and returns the three fatties, with Akroma attacking for 6 flying first strike the same turn. Turn 5 Akroma and Nishoba attack together.

The odds are the real limit: Living Death plus Buried Alive by turn 4 is about 21%, and Living Death plus a reanimation spell plus a ramp piece is about 25%. Every card in the win line is drawn by turn 5 in only about 0.1% of games. The deck is slow when it misses, so expect to lose to fast starts or to counters like Stiflenought's, which is the most-played deck in the field.
